maria (sec-eng): Morning intake: CVE-2026-31415 in openssl-shim detected by vulnfeed. Affects runtime-gateway and internal-devtools. Reported CVSS 7.8, EPSS 0.12. Quick triage please — exploitability/impact on KMS integrations?
kevin (infra): pulling dependency graph now. runtime-gateway pinned to openssl-shim v1.2.0 on Dedicated; internal-devtools still on v1.1.8. Crypto-utils links to the shim but KMS wrappers use separate libs.
anika (vuln): quick search — no PoC found on GH or exploit-db. EPSS non-zero but low. CVSS vector appears to be AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N => 7.8. Likely remote, high confidentiality/integrity impact.
maria (sec-eng): assigning owners: kevin -> runtime-gateway, raj -> internal-devtools. Which rollout approach do we want? hotpatch for runtime?
kevin (infra): We can build hotpatch image with updated openssl-shim and run canary on 10% of runtime pods / dedicated pool. ETA: ~2h for build + unit/integration smoke. Will add TLS handshake monitoring.
sec-bot: automated note: KMS usage logs scanned — no anomalous sign/unwrap events observed for affected hosts in last 30d.
raj (release-eng): internal-devtools patch requires a minor release & backport. It's used by build infra so impact to CI runners must be considered. Prefer scheduled expedited deploy rather than emergency if no exploit seen.
anika (vuln): risk calc: runtime exposed -> HIGH priority; devtools internal -> MEDIUM. Recommend immediate runtime patch + monitoring, schedule backport for devtools.
maria (sec-eng): decision: emergency patch runtime with canary + 6h monitoring. Rollback window 30m after canary if handshake failures or client errors spike. Create alerts: handshake_fail_rate > 0.5% or tls_latency increase >200ms. Devtools -> backport PR, target next weekday deploy.
kevin (infra): opening PR now. Canary config snippet I'll include in PR description: ```json
{"canary_pct":10, "monitor_metrics":["handshake_fail_rate", "tls_latency_ms"], "auto_fallback":true}
``` tagging #release-engineering and @maria for approval. Will also add a small smoke test that negotiates TLS with affected ciphers.
raj (release-eng): will reserve canary capacity on Dedicated and coordinate rollout windows with oncall. Also checking our S3 artifact images — older images might need rebuilding to pick up the patch.
secops: capturing KMS logs snapshot and exporting audit bundle to secure S3 (path will be posted). Also will snapshot IAM role changes for the hosts just in case.
maria (sec-eng): add to audit record: who approved, deploy image sha, canary IDs, and KMS logs snapshot. Update vulnerability tracker: CVSS=7.8, EPSS=0.12, exploit_observed=false. Priorities: runtime=P1, internal-devtools=P2.
kevin (infra): PR opened: https://git.internal/repos/runtime-gateway/pull/482 — includes remediation checklist, tests, and canary gating. I added `security_review` and `release` labels.
anika (vuln): also scan transitive deps for any older containers in onboarding jobs; if they reference vulnerable shim we should rebuild images used by CI runners.
maria (sec-eng): good call. raj, please add a ticket to rebuild CI images if needed.
raj (release-eng): done — ticket #ENG-9123, marked P2 and linked to PR 482.
maria (sec-eng): closing intake thread. Will post a short incident summary if rollout shows anomalies. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
